title: Example explanation not consistent with actual HTML example for header rowgroup scope
body:
The description references three groups of headers:
- The headers in the first row
- The headers with the explicit scope attributes
- The remaining headers

But since in the example HTML *all* of the headers beyond the first row have explicit scope, the second and third groups are identical and the description becomes incorrect.  

https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/tables.html#the-th-element

> The following example shows how the scope attribute's rowgroup value affects which data cells a header cell applies to.
> 
> Here is a markup fragment showing a table:​
> 
> <table>
>  <thead>
>   <tr> <th> ID <th> Measurement <th> Average <th> Maximum
>  <tbody>
>   <tr> <td> <th scope=​rowgroup> Cats <td> <td>
>   <tr> <td> 93 <th scope=​row> Legs <td> 3\.5 <td> 4
>   <tr> <td> 10 <th scope=​row> Tails <td> 1 <td> 1
>  <tbody>
>   <tr> <td> <th scope=​rowgroup> English speakers <td> <td>
>   <tr> <td> 32 <th scope=​row> Legs <td> 2\.67 <td> 4
>   <tr> <td> 35 <th scope=​row> Tails <td> 0\.33 <td> 1
> </table>
>
>
>
> The headers in the first row all apply directly down to the rows in their column.
> 
> The headers with the explicit scope attributes apply to all the cells in their row group other than the cells in the first column.
> 
> The remaining headers apply just to the cells to the right of them.

If my understanding of [the rules](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/tables.html#header-and-data-cell-semantics) is correct, then either of the following fixes would be correct:

- remove `scope=​row` from the four `th` elements with that attribute, so that "The remaining headers" refers to them as originally intended.
- Change the description to reference the explicit scope values.

I think the first option is at least slightly better since this example is specifically about the `rowgroup` scope and it would leave `rowgroup` as the only explicit scope value in the example.
